chapters.title: You Will Be My Witnesses
chapters.html:
Acts 1

The Promise of the Spirit

1In the first account, Theophilus, I wrote about all that Jesus began to do and to teach,

2until the day when He was taken up, after He had given commands through the Holy Spirit to the apostles whom He had chosen.

3To them He also showed Himself alive after His suffering by many convincing proofs, appearing to them over forty days and speaking about the kingdom of God.

4While He was eating with them, He ordered them not to leave Jerusalem, but to wait for the promise of the Father, "which you heard from Me;

5for John baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit not many days from now."

He Is Taken Up

6So when they had come together, they asked Him, "Lord, is it at this time that You are restoring the kingdom to Israel?"

7He said to them, "It is not for you to know times or seasons that the Father has set by His own authority.

8But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you, and you will be My witnesses in Jerusalem, and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the end of the earth."

9When He had said these things, as they were watching, He was lifted up, and a cloud took Him out of their sight.

10While they were gazing into heaven as He went, two men stood by them in white clothing,

11who said, "Men of Galilee, why do you stand looking into heaven? This Jesus, who has been taken up from you into heaven, will come in the same way as you saw Him go into heaven."

Matthias Chosen

12Then they returned to Jerusalem from the mount called Olivet, which is near Jerusalem, a sabbath day's journey away.

13When they had entered the city, they went up to the upper room where they were staying: Peter and John and James and Andrew, Philip and Thomas, Bartholomew and Matthew, James son of Alphaeus and Simon the Zealot, and Judas son of James.

14All these with one mind were devoting themselves to prayer, together with the women and Mary the mother of Jesus, and with His brothers.

15In those days Peter stood up among the brothers (the company of persons was in all about a hundred and twenty) and said,

16"Brothers, the Scripture had to be fulfilled, which the Holy Spirit spoke beforehand by the mouth of David about Judas, who became a guide to those who arrested Jesus.

17For he was counted among us and was allotted his share in this ministry."

18(This man acquired a field with the reward of his wrongdoing; and falling headlong he burst open in the middle, and all his insides poured out.

19It became known to all who live in Jerusalem, so that the field was called in their own language Akeldama, that is, Field of Blood.)

20"For it is written in the book of Psalms, 'Let his homestead be made desolate, and let no one live in it,' and, 'Let another take his office.'

21So one of the men who have accompanied us during all the time that the Lord Jesus went in and out among us,

22beginning from the baptism of John until the day when He was taken up from us, must become with us a witness of His resurrection."

23They put forward two, Joseph called Barsabbas, who was surnamed Justus, and Matthias.

24They prayed and said, "You, Lord, who know the hearts of all, show which one of these two You have chosen

25to take the place in this ministry and apostleship from which Judas turned aside to go to his own place."

26They cast lots for them, and the lot fell on Matthias, and he was counted with the eleven apostles.

Notes

  • vv1–5 "In the first account, Theophilus… all that Jesus began to do and to teach… the promise of the Father… baptized with the Holy Spirit" — the first account is the Gospel of Luke, written for you, most excellent Theophilus (Luke 1:3). Ērxato, began: what Jesus began, His apostles carry on. The last words of Luke are here again, I am sending the promise of My Father upon you (Luke 24:49), and John's, He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire (Luke 3:16). Synalizomenos, while He was eating with them, may also be while He was staying with them.

  • vv6–8 "restoring the kingdom to Israel… times or seasons… you will be My witnesses… to the end of the earth" — apokathistaneis, restoring, the verb the Greek of Malachi uses of Elijah, who will turn the heart of fathers to sons (Malachi 4:6; 4:5 in the Greek). To the end of the earth is Isaiah's servant, a light for the nations, that My deliverance may reach to the end of the earth (Isaiah 49:6).

  • vv9–11 "He was lifted up, and a cloud took Him… two men… in white clothing… will come in the same way" — Luke has the same day ending at Bethany, He parted from them and was carried up into heaven (Luke 24:51). Elijah went up in a whirlwind to heaven while Elisha watched (2 Kings 2:11). Two men, as at the tomb (Luke 24:4). The Son of Man comes with the clouds of heaven (Daniel 7:13).

  • vv12–14 "the mount called Olivet… a sabbath day's journey… the upper room… Mary the mother of Jesus, and with His brothers" — Elaiōn, Olivet, the Mount of Olives. A sabbath day's journey, the distance one might walk on the sabbath. The eleven are named as in Luke 6:14–16, without Judas Iscariot. Homothymadon, with one mind, a word Acts uses often (2:46; 4:24).

  • vv15–17 "about a hundred and twenty… the Holy Spirit spoke beforehand by the mouth of David… allotted his share" — onomatōn, persons, word for word names. Elachen ton klēron, was allotted his share, word for word obtained the lot, as Matthias will (v26).

  • vv18–19 "acquired a field with the reward of his wrongdoing… falling headlong he burst open… Akeldama, that is, Field of Blood" — the writer's aside to the reader, set in parentheses: in their own language is not how Peter would speak to the people of Jerusalem. Matthew tells it otherwise: Judas hanged himself, and the priests bought the Field of Blood with the silver (Matthew 27:5–8). Prēnēs genomenos, falling headlong. Hakeldamach is Aramaic, field of blood.

  • v20 "Let his homestead be made desolate… Let another take his office" — Psalm 69:25, Let their camp be desolate; let no one live in their tents, made singular; the Greek of the Psalm has epaulis, homestead, as here. Psalm 109:8, let another take his office, as the Greek, episkopē, office, the word later used of an overseer, a bishop.

  • vv21–26 "went in and out among us… a witness of His resurrection… who know the hearts of all… They cast lots… Matthias" — went in and out, as Moses asked for one who will go out before them and come in before them (Numbers 27:17). Kardiognōsta, who know the hearts, as the LORD looks at the heart (1 Samuel 16:7). The lot was the old way of finding the LORD's choice, as the land was divided by lot (Numbers 26:55). Twelve again, for the twelve tribes (Luke 22:30).

chapters.title: The Day of Pentecost
chapters.html:
Acts 2

The Spirit Comes

1When the day of Pentecost had come, they were all together in one place.

2Suddenly there came from heaven a sound like a rushing, violent wind, and it filled the whole house where they were sitting.

3Tongues as of fire appeared to them, divided, and one rested on each of them.

4They were all filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak in other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance.

5Now there were Jews living in Jerusalem, devout men from every nation under heaven.

6When this sound came, the crowd gathered and was bewildered, because each one heard them speaking in his own language.

7They were amazed and astonished, saying, "Are not all these who are speaking Galileans?

8How is it that each of us hears them in his own native language?

9Parthians and Medes and Elamites, and those who live in Mesopotamia, Judea and Cappadocia, Pontus and Asia,

10Phrygia and Pamphylia, Egypt and the parts of Libya near Cyrene, and visitors from Rome,

11both Jews and proselytes, Cretans and Arabs — we hear them telling in our own tongues the mighty works of God."

12All were amazed and perplexed, saying to one another, "What does this mean?"

13But others mocked and said, "They are full of new wine."

Peter Speaks

14But Peter, standing with the eleven, raised his voice and addressed them: "Men of Judea and all who live in Jerusalem, let this be known to you, and listen to my words.

15These men are not drunk, as you suppose, for it is only the third hour of the day.

16But this is what was spoken through the prophet Joel:

17'And it shall come to pass in the last days, says God, that I will pour out My Spirit on all flesh; your sons and your daughters will prophesy, your young men will see visions, and your old men will dream dreams.

18Even on My male servants and My female servants in those days I will pour out My Spirit, and they will prophesy.

19I will give wonders in the heavens above and signs on the earth below, blood and fire and vapor of smoke.

20The sun will be turned to darkness and the moon to blood, before the great and glorious day of the Lord comes.

21And it shall come to pass that everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved.'

22"Men of Israel, hear these words: Jesus of Nazareth, a man attested to you by God with mighty works and wonders and signs that God did through Him in your midst, as you yourselves know —

23this man, handed over by the set plan and foreknowledge of God, you nailed up and killed by the hands of lawless men.

24God raised Him up, releasing Him from the pangs of death, because it was not possible for Him to be held by it.

25For David says about Him, 'I saw the Lord always before me, for He is at my right hand, so that I will not be shaken.

26Therefore my heart was glad, and my tongue rejoiced; my flesh also will dwell in hope.

27For You will not abandon my soul to Hades, nor let Your Holy One see decay.

28You have made known to me the paths of life; You will fill me with gladness in Your presence.'

29"Brothers, I may speak to you with confidence about the patriarch David, that he both died and was buried, and his tomb is with us to this day.

30Being a prophet, and knowing that God had sworn to him with an oath to seat one of the fruit of his body on his throne,

31he foresaw and spoke of the resurrection of the Messiah, that He was not abandoned to Hades, nor did His flesh see decay.

32This Jesus God raised up, and of that we are all witnesses.

33Being therefore exalted at the right hand of God, and having received from the Father the promise of the Holy Spirit, He has poured out this that you see and hear.

34For David did not go up into the heavens, but he himself says, 'The Lord said to my Lord, Sit at My right hand,

35until I make Your enemies a footstool for Your feet.'

36Let all the house of Israel therefore know for certain that God has made Him both Lord and Messiah, this Jesus whom you crucified."

Three Thousand Added

37When they heard this, they were cut to the heart, and said to Peter and the rest of the apostles, "Brothers, what shall we do?"

38Peter said to them, "Repent, and let each of you be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins; and you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit.

39For the promise is for you and for your children and for all who are far off, as many as the Lord our God will call to Himself."

40With many other words he bore witness and urged them, saying, "Be saved from this crooked generation."

41So those who received his word were baptized, and that day about three thousand souls were added.

42They devoted themselves to the apostles' teaching and to the fellowship, to the breaking of bread and to the prayers.

The Life of the Believers

43Awe came upon every soul, and many wonders and signs were done through the apostles.

44All who believed were together and had all things in common.

45They sold their possessions and goods and distributed them to all, as anyone had need.

46Day by day, devoting themselves with one mind to the temple, and breaking bread in their homes, they shared their food with gladness and simplicity of heart,

47praising God and having favor with all the people. The Lord added to their number day by day those who were being saved.

Notes

  • vv1–4 "the day of Pentecost… a sound like a rushing, violent wind… Tongues as of fire… began to speak in other tongues" — Pentēkostē, Pentecost, the fiftieth day, the Feast of Weeks, when the law says you shall count fifty days, and you shall present a new grain offering (Leviticus 23:16). Pnoē, wind, also breath, of the same root as pneuma. Fire came down on Sinai, because the LORD had come down on it in fire (Exodus 19:18). John said the one to come will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire (Luke 3:16). Glōssai, tongues, both of the fire and of speech.

  • vv5–13 "devout men from every nation under heaven… each one heard them speaking in his own language… They are full of new wine" — at Babel the LORD confused the lip of all the earth… and scattered them (Genesis 11:9); here the scattered nations hear one message, each in its own speech. Dialektos, language. The list runs from the east (Parthia, Media, Elam) round to Rome and back to Crete and Arabia. Proselytoi, proselytes, Gentiles who had become Jews. Gleukos, new wine, sweet wine.

  • vv14–21 "the third hour… this is what was spoken through the prophet Joel… in the last days… everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved" — the third hour, about nine in the morning. The words are Joel 2:28–32; Peter's Greek has in the last days for afterward, says God, and and they will prophesy (v18), and adds signs… below. Joel's before the great and fearful day of the LORD is great and glorious here, as in the Greek of Joel. Joel's will escape is will be saved, as the Greek of Joel has it. The Lord in v21 is the LORD of Joel; v36 gives the name to Jesus.

  • vv22–24 "a man attested to you by God… handed over by the set plan and foreknowledge of God… releasing Him from the pangs of death" — prospēxantes, nailed up, fastened to the cross. Anomōn, lawless men, those without the law. Tas ōdinas tou thanatou, the pangs of death, word for word the birth pains of death, as the Greek of Psalm 18:4 (17:5 in the Greek numbering) has ōdines thanatou, where the Hebrew has The cords of death surrounded me.

  • vv25–31 "I saw the Lord always before me… You will not abandon my soul to Hades, nor let Your Holy One see decay… one of the fruit of his body on his throne" — Psalm 16:8–11 in the words of its Greek (15:8–11 in the Greek numbering). The Hebrew has I have set the LORD always before me, my glory rejoices where the Greek has my tongue, and nor let Your faithful one see the pit, where the Greek has diaphthoran, decay. David was buried in the City of David (1 Kings 2:10). God swore One of the fruit of your body I will set on your throne (Psalm 132:11).

  • vv32–36 "exalted at the right hand of God… The Lord said to my Lord… both Lord and Messiah" — Psalm 110:1, as Jesus quoted it (Luke 20:42–43). He has poured out, the verb of Joel, I will pour out (v17): what God promised, the exalted Jesus does. Kyrion kai christon, Lord and Messiah.

  • vv37–42 "cut to the heart… Repent, and let each of you be baptized… for all who are far off… this crooked generation… three thousand" — katenygēsan, were cut, pierced. Peace, peace, to the far and to the near (Isaiah 57:19). A crooked and twisted generation (Deuteronomy 32:5). Tē koinōnia, the fellowship, a sharing in common. Tē klasei tou artou, the breaking of bread, as at Emmaus (Luke 24:35).

  • vv43–47 "had all things in common… with gladness and simplicity of heart… those who were being saved" — hapanta koina, all things in common. Aphelotēti, simplicity, a smooth, single heart. Tous sōzomenous, those who were being saved, Joel's will be saved (v21) coming true day by day.

chapters.title: In the Name of Jesus, Walk
chapters.html:
Acts 3

The Lame Man Healed

1Peter and John were going up to the temple at the hour of prayer, the ninth hour.

2A man lame from his mother's womb was being carried in; they would set him down every day at the gate of the temple called Beautiful, to ask alms of those going into the temple.

3When he saw Peter and John about to go into the temple, he asked to receive alms.

4Peter looked straight at him, with John, and said, "Look at us."

5He gave them his attention, expecting to receive something from them.

6But Peter said, "I have no silver and gold, but what I have I give you: in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, walk!"

7He took him by the right hand and raised him up; and at once his feet and ankles were made strong.

8Leaping up, he stood and began to walk, and he went with them into the temple, walking and leaping and praising God.

9All the people saw him walking and praising God,

10and they recognized him as the one who used to sit begging for alms at the Beautiful Gate of the temple; and they were filled with wonder and amazement at what had happened to him.

Peter Speaks in Solomon's Colonnade

11While he was holding on to Peter and John, all the people ran together to them in the colonnade called Solomon's, utterly astounded.

12When Peter saw it, he answered the people: "Men of Israel, why do you wonder at this, or why do you stare at us, as though by our own power or godliness we had made him walk?

13The God of Abraham and of Isaac and of Jacob, the God of our fathers, has glorified His servant Jesus, whom you handed over and denied before Pilate, when he had decided to release Him.

14But you denied the Holy and Righteous One and asked for a murderer to be granted to you,

15and you killed the Author of life, whom God raised from the dead. Of this we are witnesses.

16By faith in His name, His name has made this man strong, whom you see and know; and the faith that comes through Him has given him this perfect health in the presence of you all.

17"Now, brothers, I know that you acted in ignorance, as did also your rulers.

18But what God foretold by the mouth of all the prophets, that His Messiah would suffer, He has fulfilled in this way.

19Repent therefore, and turn back, so that your sins may be wiped out,

20that times of refreshing may come from the presence of the Lord, and that He may send the Messiah appointed for you, Jesus,

21whom heaven must receive until the times of the restoring of all things, of which God spoke by the mouth of His holy prophets from of old.

22Moses said, 'The Lord your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your brothers. You shall listen to him in everything he says to you.

23And it shall come to pass that every soul that does not listen to that prophet shall be utterly cut off from the people.'

24All the prophets who have spoken, from Samuel and those who came after him, also proclaimed these days.

25You are the sons of the prophets and of the covenant that God made with your fathers, saying to Abraham, 'In your seed all the families of the earth shall be blessed.'

26God, having raised up His servant, sent Him to you first, to bless you by turning each of you from your wicked ways."

Notes

  • vv1–3 "the hour of prayer, the ninth hour… lame from his mother's womb… the gate of the temple called Beautiful" — the ninth hour, about three in the afternoon. Hōraia, Beautiful, the gate is named only here. Eleēmosynē, alms, a gift of mercy.

  • vv4–8 "Look at us… I have no silver and gold… in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, walk!… walking and leaping and praising God" — atenisas, looked straight at. The prophets saw the day when the lame will leap like a deer (Isaiah 35:6).

  • vv11–16 "the colonnade called Solomon's… has glorified His servant Jesus… the Holy and Righteous One… the Author of life" — the colonnade where Jesus walked (John 10:23). The God of Abraham and of Isaac and of Jacob is the name God gave at the bush (Exodus 3:15). Edoxasen ton paida autou, has glorified His servant: Isaiah's servant will rise high and be lifted up, and the Greek of Isaiah has ho pais mou… doxasthēsetai, My servant… will be glorified (Isaiah 52:13). The righteous one, My servant (Isaiah 53:11). Archēgos, Author, also leader, pioneer, the one who begins and leads: they asked for a man who took life and killed the one who gives it.

  • vv17–21 "you acted in ignorance… that His Messiah would suffer… times of refreshing… the restoring of all things" — Jesus prayed, Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing (Luke 23:34). Exaleiphthēnai, wiped out, as writing is wiped from a tablet. Apokatastaseōs, restoring, the word of 1:6, restoring the kingdom to Israel.

  • vv22–23 "a prophet like me… every soul that does not listen to that prophet shall be utterly cut off" — Deuteronomy 18:15, A prophet from among you, from your brothers, like me, the LORD your God will raise up for you. To him you shall listen; then 18:19, whoever will not listen to My words… I Myself will require it of him, which Peter gives in the words of the law's cut off from his people (Leviticus 23:29).

  • vv24–26 "from Samuel… In your seed all the families of the earth shall be blessed… to bless you by turning each of you" — Samuel was the first of the prophets, established as a prophet of the LORD (1 Samuel 3:20). The promise to Abraham, In your seed all the nations of the earth shall bless themselves (Genesis 22:18), is given with families, as Genesis 12:3, all the families of the ground shall be blessed. Anastēsas, having raised up, the verb of v22, will raise up… a prophet, and of the resurrection.

speech.text: Acts 3
The Lame Man Healed
Peter and John were going up to the temple at the hour of prayer, the ninth hour.
A man lame from his mother's womb was being carried in; they would set him down every day at the gate of the temple called Beautiful, to ask alms of those going into the temple.
When he saw Peter and John about to go into the temple, he asked to receive alms.
Peter looked straight at him, with John, and said, "Look at us."
He gave them his attention, expecting to receive something from them.
But Peter said, "I have no silver and gold, but what I have I give you: in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, walk!"
He took him by the right hand and raised him up; and at once his feet and ankles were made strong.
Leaping up, he stood and began to walk, and he went with them into the temple, walking and leaping and praising God.
All the people saw him walking and praising God,
and they recognized him as the one who used to sit begging for alms at the Beautiful Gate of the temple; and they were filled with wonder and amazement at what had happened to him.
Peter Speaks in Solomon's Colonnade
While he was holding on to Peter and John, all the people ran together to them in the colonnade called Solomon's, utterly astounded.
When Peter saw it, he answered the people: "Men of Israel, why do you wonder at this, or why do you stare at us, as though by our own power or godliness we had made him walk?
The God of Abraham and of Isaac and of Jacob, the God of our fathers, has glorified His servant Jesus, whom you handed over and denied before Pilate, when he had decided to release Him.
But you denied the Holy and Righteous One and asked for a murderer to be granted to you,
and you killed the Author of life, whom God raised from the dead. Of this we are witnesses.
By faith in His name, His name has made this man strong, whom you see and know; and the faith that comes through Him has given him this perfect health in the presence of you all.
"Now, brothers, I know that you acted in ignorance, as did also your rulers.
But what God foretold by the mouth of all the prophets, that His Messiah would suffer, He has fulfilled in this way.
Repent therefore, and turn back, so that your sins may be wiped out,
that times of refreshing may come from the presence of the Lord, and that He may send the Messiah appointed for you, Jesus,
whom heaven must receive until the times of the restoring of all things, of which God spoke by the mouth of His holy prophets from of old.
Moses said, 'The Lord your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your brothers. You shall listen to him in everything he says to you.
And it shall come to pass that every soul that does not listen to that prophet shall be utterly cut off from the people.'
All the prophets who have spoken, from Samuel and those who came after him, also proclaimed these days.
You are the sons of the prophets and of the covenant that God made with your fathers, saying to Abraham, 'In your seed all the families of the earth shall be blessed.'
God, having raised up His servant, sent Him to you first, to bless you by turning each of you from your wicked ways."

chapters.title: No Other Name
chapters.html:
Acts 4

Peter and John Arrested

1While they were speaking to the people, the priests and the captain of the temple and the Sadducees came upon them,

2greatly annoyed because they were teaching the people and proclaiming in Jesus the resurrection from the dead.

3They laid hands on them and put them in custody until the next day, for it was already evening.

4But many of those who had heard the word believed, and the number of the men came to about five thousand.

5The next day their rulers and elders and scribes gathered in Jerusalem,

6with Annas the high priest and Caiaphas and John and Alexander, and all who were of the high-priestly family.

7When they had set them in the middle, they inquired, "By what power or by what name did you do this?"

8Then Peter, filled with the Holy Spirit, said to them, "Rulers of the people and elders,

9if we are being examined today about a good deed done to a sick man, by what means this man has been made well,

10let it be known to all of you and to all the people of Israel that by the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, whom you crucified, whom God raised from the dead — by Him this man stands before you well.

11This Jesus is the stone that was rejected by you, the builders, which has become the head of the corner.

12There is salvation in no one else; for there is no other name under heaven given among men by which we must be saved."

13When they saw the boldness of Peter and John, and perceived that they were unlettered and ordinary men, they were amazed; and they recognized that they had been with Jesus.

14Seeing the man who had been healed standing beside them, they had nothing to say in reply.

15So they ordered them to go outside the council, and conferred with one another,

16saying, "What shall we do with these men? For that a notable sign has been done through them is plain to all who live in Jerusalem, and we cannot deny it.

17But so that it spreads no further among the people, let us warn them to speak no more to anyone in this name."

18So they called them and commanded them not to speak or teach at all in the name of Jesus.

19But Peter and John answered them, "Whether it is right in the sight of God to listen to you rather than to God, you must judge;

20for we cannot but speak of what we have seen and heard."

21When they had threatened them further, they let them go, finding no way to punish them, because of the people; for all were glorifying God for what had happened.

22For the man on whom this sign of healing had been done was more than forty years old.

The Believers Pray

23When they were released, they went to their own people and reported all that the chief priests and the elders had said to them.

24When they heard it, they raised their voices to God with one mind and said, "Sovereign Lord, You who made the heaven and the earth and the sea and everything in them,

25who by the Holy Spirit, through the mouth of our father David, Your servant, said, 'Why did the nations rage, and the peoples plot in vain?

26The kings of the earth took their stand, and the rulers gathered together against the Lord and against His Anointed.'

27For truly in this city there gathered together against Your holy servant Jesus, whom You anointed, both Herod and Pontius Pilate, with the nations and the peoples of Israel,

28to do whatever Your hand and Your plan had decided beforehand should take place.

29Now, Lord, look on their threats, and grant to Your servants to speak Your word with all boldness,

30while You stretch out Your hand to heal, and signs and wonders are done through the name of Your holy servant Jesus."

31When they had prayed, the place where they were gathered together was shaken, and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit and spoke the word of God with boldness.

All Things in Common

32The whole company of those who believed was of one heart and soul, and no one said that any of the things he possessed was his own, but they had all things in common.

33With great power the apostles gave their witness to the resurrection of the Lord Jesus, and great grace was upon them all.

34There was no needy person among them, for all who were owners of lands or houses sold them and brought the proceeds of what was sold

35and laid it at the apostles' feet; and it was distributed to each as anyone had need.

36Joseph, who was called by the apostles Barnabas (which translated means Son of Encouragement), a Levite, a native of Cyprus,

37sold a field that belonged to him, brought the money and laid it at the apostles' feet.

Notes

  • vv1–4 "the captain of the temple and the Sadducees… proclaiming in Jesus the resurrection from the dead… about five thousand" — ho stratēgos tou hierou, the captain of the temple; Luke has officers of the temple (Luke 22:52). The Sadducees are those who say that there is no resurrection (Luke 20:27). Andrōn, men, the men counted.

  • vv5–12 "Annas the high priest and Caiaphas… By what power or by what name… the stone that was rejected by you, the builders… no other name under heaven" — the men of the night of the trial (John 18:13, 24). Sesōstai, has been made well, word for word has been saved: the same verb in v12, we must be saved. The stone is Psalm 118:22, The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone, as Jesus quoted it (Luke 20:17); Peter says rejected by you, the builders, and exouthenētheis, rejected, word for word counted as nothing.

  • vv13–22 "the boldness of Peter and John… unlettered and ordinary men… we cannot but speak of what we have seen and heard" — parrēsia, boldness, plainness of speech, four times in this chapter (vv13, 29, 31). Agrammatoi, unlettered, untrained in the scribes' learning; idiōtai, ordinary men, private persons. Jesus promised them a mouth and wisdom that none of your opponents will be able to withstand or contradict (Luke 21:15). More than forty years old, and lame from birth (3:2).

  • vv23–28 "Sovereign Lord, You who made the heaven and the earth and the sea… Why did the nations rage… against the Lord and against His Anointed" — Despota, Sovereign Lord, the master of a house. The Maker of heaven and earth, the sea and everything in them (Psalm 146:6). The Psalm is Psalm 2:1–2 in the words of its Greek, Why do the nations rage, and the peoples plot in vain? The kings of the earth take their stand, where the Greek has synēchthēsan, gathered together, for the Hebrew's take counsel together. Christou, Anointed, and echrisas, You anointed (v27): the LORD has anointed me (Isaiah 61:1), as Jesus read it in Nazareth (Luke 4:18). Herod and Pilate stand together, as in Luke 23:12.

  • vv29–31 "look on their threats… with all boldness… the place… was shaken" — Esaleuthē, was shaken, as Sinai trembled violently when the LORD came down (Exodus 19:18).

  • vv32–37 "of one heart and soul… all things in common… no needy person among them… Barnabas (which translated means Son of Encouragement)" — the law's hope, there will be no needy among you (Deuteronomy 15:4), endeēs, needy, the word of the Greek of that verse. Huios paraklēseōs, Son of Encouragement, the root of paraklētos (John 14:16); bar is Aramaic for son. A Levite with a field: the law gave the Levites no share of land in Israel (Numbers 18:20).

chapters.title: We Must Obey God
chapters.html:
Acts 5

Ananias and Sapphira

1But a man named Ananias, with his wife Sapphira, sold a piece of property,

2and with his wife's knowledge he kept back some of the price, and brought only a part and laid it at the apostles' feet.

3But Peter said, "Ananias, why has Satan filled your heart to lie to the Holy Spirit and to keep back some of the price of the land?

4While it remained unsold, did it not remain your own? After it was sold, was it not at your disposal? Why have you set this deed in your heart? You have not lied to men but to God."

5When Ananias heard these words, he fell down and breathed his last; and great fear came on all who heard of it.

6The young men got up, wrapped him up, carried him out and buried him.

7About three hours later his wife came in, not knowing what had happened.

8Peter said to her, "Tell me whether you sold the land for so much." She said, "Yes, for so much."

9Peter said to her, "Why have you agreed together to test the Spirit of the Lord? The feet of those who have buried your husband are at the door, and they will carry you out."

10At once she fell down at his feet and breathed her last. When the young men came in, they found her dead, and they carried her out and buried her beside her husband.

11Great fear came on the whole church and on all who heard of these things.

Signs and Wonders

12Many signs and wonders were done among the people by the hands of the apostles; and they were all together with one mind in Solomon's Colonnade.

13None of the rest dared to join them, but the people held them in high honor.

14More and more believers were added to the Lord, multitudes of both men and women,

15so that they even carried the sick out into the streets and laid them on cots and mats, so that as Peter came by at least his shadow might fall on some of them.

16The crowds also gathered from the towns around Jerusalem, bringing the sick and those troubled by unclean spirits, and they were all healed.

The Apostles Before the Council

17But the high priest rose up, and all who were with him, the party of the Sadducees, and they were filled with jealousy.

18They laid hands on the apostles and put them in the public prison.

19But during the night an angel of the Lord opened the doors of the prison, brought them out and said,

20"Go, stand in the temple and speak to the people all the words of this Life."

21When they heard this, they entered the temple at daybreak and began to teach. When the high priest and those with him arrived, they called together the council, all the senate of the sons of Israel, and sent to the prison to have them brought.

22But when the officers came, they did not find them in the prison, so they returned and reported,

23"We found the prison securely locked and the guards standing at the doors, but when we opened them, we found no one inside."

24When the captain of the temple and the chief priests heard these words, they were at a loss about them, wondering what this would come to.

25Someone came and told them, "The men whom you put in prison are standing in the temple and teaching the people."

26Then the captain went with the officers and brought them, but without force, for they were afraid of being stoned by the people.

27When they had brought them, they set them before the council. The high priest questioned them,

28saying, "We strictly ordered you not to teach in this name, yet you have filled Jerusalem with your teaching and intend to bring this man's blood on us."

29But Peter and the apostles answered, "We must obey God rather than men.

30The God of our fathers raised up Jesus, whom you killed by hanging Him on a tree.

31God exalted Him at His right hand as Leader and Savior, to give repentance to Israel and forgiveness of sins.

32We are witnesses of these things, and so is the Holy Spirit, whom God has given to those who obey Him."

Gamaliel's Advice

33When they heard this, they were furious and wanted to kill them.

34But a Pharisee in the council named Gamaliel, a teacher of the law held in honor by all the people, stood up and gave orders to put the men outside for a little while.

35Then he said to them, "Men of Israel, take care what you are about to do with these men.

36For some time ago Theudas rose up, claiming to be somebody, and a number of men, about four hundred, joined him. He was killed, and all who followed him were scattered and came to nothing.

37After him Judas the Galilean rose up in the days of the registration and drew away people after him. He too perished, and all who followed him were dispersed.

38So in the present case I tell you, keep away from these men and let them alone; for if this plan or this work is of men, it will come to nothing;

39but if it is of God, you will not be able to overthrow them. You might even be found fighting against God!" They were persuaded by him,

40and when they had called in the apostles, they beat them and ordered them not to speak in the name of Jesus, and let them go.

41So they went out from the presence of the council, rejoicing that they had been counted worthy to suffer dishonor for the Name.

42Every day, in the temple and from house to house, they did not cease teaching and proclaiming the good news that the Messiah is Jesus.

Notes

  • vv1–6 "kept back some of the price… why has Satan filled your heart… You have not lied to men but to God… breathed his last" — enosphisato, kept back, the verb the Greek of Joshua uses of Achan, who took some of what was devoted (Joshua 7:1), enosphisanto. Pseusasthai se to pneuma to hagion… ouk epseusō anthrōpois alla tō theō, to lie to the Holy Spirit… not… to men but to God: lying to the Spirit is lying to God. Exepsyxen, breathed his last. Satan entered into Judas (Luke 22:3).

  • vv7–11 "to test the Spirit of the Lord… Great fear came on the whole church" — peirasai, to test, as Israel tested the LORD at Massah (Exodus 17:2); You shall not test the LORD your God (Deuteronomy 6:16). Ekklēsia, church, its first use in Acts: the assembly, the word the Greek of Deuteronomy uses for Israel's assembly at Horeb (Deuteronomy 9:10, in the Greek, tēs ekklēsias).

  • vv12–16 "Solomon's Colonnade… None of the rest dared to join them… at least his shadow might fall" — kollasthai, to join, to be glued to. Episkiasē, might fall on, overshadow, the verb of the Spirit on Mary, the power of the Most High will overshadow you (Luke 1:35).

  • vv17–26 "the party of the Sadducees… filled with jealousy… an angel of the Lord opened the doors… the words of this Life" — hairesis, party, a school of thought, the root of heresy. Angelos kyriou, an angel of the Lord, as at Jesus' birth (Luke 2:9). Tēs zōēs tautēs, this Life, the life the apostles preach.

  • vv27–32 "intend to bring this man's blood on us… We must obey God rather than men… hanging Him on a tree… Leader and Savior" — at the trial the people said His blood be on us (Matthew 27:25). Peitharchein, obey, obey a ruler. Kremasantes epi xylou, hanging Him on a tree, the words of the law, you hang him on a tree (Deuteronomy 21:22), for one who is hanged is a curse of God (Deuteronomy 21:23). Archēgos, Leader, as 3:15.

  • vv33–39 "they were furious… Gamaliel… Theudas… Judas the Galilean in the days of the registration… fighting against God" — dieprionto, were furious, word for word were sawn through. The registration is the census of the time of Quirinius (Luke 2:2). Theomachoi, fighting against God, one word.

  • vv40–42 "they beat them… rejoicing that they had been counted worthy to suffer dishonor for the Name… the Messiah is Jesus" — as Jesus said, Rejoice in that day and leap for joy (Luke 6:23), for My name's sake (Luke 21:12). Hyper tou onomatos, for the Name, the name of 3:16 and 4:12. Euangelizomenoi ton christon Iēsoun, proclaiming the good news that the Messiah is Jesus, or proclaiming Jesus as the Messiah.

chapters.title: The Seven
chapters.html:
Acts 6

Seven Chosen to Serve

1In those days, when the disciples were increasing in number, the Hellenists began to grumble against the Hebrews, because their widows were being overlooked in the daily distribution.

2So the twelve called together the whole company of the disciples and said, "It is not right for us to leave the word of God to serve tables.

3So, brothers, pick out from among you seven men of good repute, full of the Spirit and of wisdom, whom we may appoint to this duty.

4But we will devote ourselves to prayer and to the ministry of the word."

5What they said pleased the whole company, and they chose Stephen, a man full of faith and of the Holy Spirit, and Philip, Prochorus, Nicanor, Timon, Parmenas, and Nicolaus, a proselyte of Antioch.

6They set these before the apostles, who prayed and laid their hands on them.

7The word of God kept spreading, and the number of the disciples in Jerusalem increased greatly, and a great many of the priests became obedient to the faith.

Stephen Seized

8Stephen, full of grace and power, was doing great wonders and signs among the people.

9But some of those from the synagogue called the Synagogue of the Freedmen, and of the Cyrenians and Alexandrians, and of those from Cilicia and Asia, rose up and disputed with Stephen.

10But they could not withstand the wisdom and the Spirit with which he spoke.

11Then they secretly put forward men who said, "We have heard him speak blasphemous words against Moses and God."

12They stirred up the people and the elders and the scribes, and they came upon him, seized him and brought him before the council.

13They set up false witnesses who said, "This man never stops speaking words against this holy place and the Law;

14for we have heard him say that this Jesus of Nazareth will destroy this place and will change the customs that Moses handed down to us."

15All who sat in the council, looking intently at him, saw that his face was like the face of an angel.

Notes

  • vv1–4 "the Hellenists… the Hebrews… their widows were being overlooked… to serve tables… the ministry of the word" — Hellēnistai, Hellenists, Jews whose speech was Greek; Hebraioi, Hebrews, Jews of the land. Egeneto gongysmos, began to grumble, the grumbling of Israel in the wilderness (Exodus 16:2). Diakonia, distribution, word for word service, the same word as the ministry of the word (v4): the serving of tables and the serving of the word.

  • vv3–6 "seven men of good repute, full of the Spirit and of wisdom… laid their hands on them" — Moses was told to choose capable men who fear God, men of truth (Exodus 18:21), men who are wise, discerning and known among your tribes (Deuteronomy 1:13). All seven names are Greek. Prosēlytos, proselyte, a Gentile who had become a Jew. Moses leaned his hands on Joshua, a man in whom is the spirit (Numbers 27:18, 23).

  • v7 "The word of God kept spreading… a great many of the priests became obedient to the faith" — ēuxanen, kept spreading, word for word was growing, as a plant grows, the first of the book's notes of growth (12:24; 19:20).

  • vv8–10 "full of grace and power… the Synagogue of the Freedmen… could not withstand the wisdom and the Spirit" — Libertinōn, Freedmen, a Latin word in Greek letters, freed slaves or their sons. As Jesus promised, none of your opponents will be able to withstand or contradict (Luke 21:15).

  • vv11–15 "blasphemous words against Moses and God… false witnesses… will destroy this place… the face of an angel" — the charge against Jesus at His trial, I will destroy this sanctuary (Mark 14:58), when some gave false testimony against Him (Mark 14:57). Ethē, customs. The face of an angel: when Moses came down from the mountain the skin of his face had grown horns from speaking with Him (Exodus 34:29).

So the twelve called together the whole company of the disciples and said, "It is not right for us to leave the word of God to serve tables.
So, brothers, pick out from among you seven men of good repute, full of the Spirit and of wisdom, whom we may appoint to this duty.
But we will devote ourselves to prayer and to the ministry of the word."
What they said pleased the whole company, and they chose Stephen, a man full of faith and of the Holy Spirit, and Philip, Prochorus, Nicanor, Timon, Parmenas, and Nicolaus, a proselyte of Antioch.
They set these before the apostles, who prayed and laid their hands on them.
The word of God kept spreading, and the number of the disciples in Jerusalem increased greatly, and a great many of the priests became obedient to the faith.
Stephen Seized
Stephen, full of grace and power, was doing great wonders and signs among the people.
But some of those from the synagogue called the Synagogue of the Freedmen, and of the Cyrenians and Alexandrians, and of those from Cilicia and Asia, rose up and disputed with Stephen.
But they could not withstand the wisdom and the Spirit with which he spoke.
Then they secretly put forward men who said, "We have heard him speak blasphemous words against Moses and God."
They stirred up the people and the elders and the scribes, and they came upon him, seized him and brought him before the council.
They set up false witnesses who said, "This man never stops speaking words against this holy place and the Law;
for we have heard him say that this Jesus of Nazareth will destroy this place and will change the customs that Moses handed down to us."
All who sat in the council, looking intently at him, saw that his face was like the face of an angel.
